leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used for a privacy-preserving interface between an agent's conversation-derived classification and a shared globe, avoiding transcript transfer and exposing only aggregate energy categories.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes two page tools that accept classified token energy while rejecting transcript-like keys.
Multiple chats contribute to one shared planet without storing conversation text.
execution_rationale: The live globe loaded and its purpose was identifiable, but the attempted place inspection hung and no post-action state or central workflow completion was verified.
execution_evidence: Live observation says the globe and growth notice were visible.
Central click interaction was unclear and no after screenshot/state was confirmed.
impact_rationale: The concept offers meaningful privacy and shared-visualization value for turning otherwise inaccessible conversational activity into a non-text collective artifact, though practical impact is not demonstrated beyond the concept.
impact_evidence: Submission emphasizes no transcript storage and aggregate-only reporting.
Shared globe is designed to accumulate signals from several chats.
creativity_rationale: A shared planetary visualization of AI-chat energy, coupled with privacy constraints and agent-side classification, is an unusual and coherent WebMCP use.
creativity_evidence: Joy, work, strain, and other categories map to distinct planetary terrain.
The site explicitly rejects sensitive transcript-shaped inputs.
s2_notes: Live site was reachable and concept matched the visible globe, but the core WebMCP reporting/inspection flow was not verified.
advance_reason: Strong concept but insufficient live verification of the central interaction.

leverage_rationale: Ladder makes WebMCP the human control plane for consequential page actions: writes run against a fork, produce an editable proof, and replay under a rollback guard.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes two read and two write tools, with writes following fork, proof, human narrowing, and guarded replay.
Video transcript describes partial application, refusals, re-planning, and rollback of an unproved write.
execution_rationale: The live landing page coherently explained the fork/proof/cut-down/rollback model and a partially applied example, but the attempted proof-tab interaction failed and no live action execution was observed.
execution_evidence: Live observation found a reachable polished page with visible proof concepts and a partially applied example.
Opening THE PROOF tab produced no usable interactive elements or changed state.
impact_rationale: A human-reviewable, selectively applicable and rollback-protected action layer addresses a major safety gap for agents changing real records, with applicability beyond the demonstrated domain.
impact_evidence: Submission frames the system as a consequential-action control plane.
Transcript demonstrates preserving valid changes while refusing selected records and rolling back unexpected writes.
creativity_rationale: The editable proof and exact re-execution under a guard are a distinctive WebMCP-native answer to the all-or-nothing nature of agent tool calls, and the engine is presented as domain-portable.
creativity_evidence: Human can cut down a proposed set while figures and receipt update.
Unexpected writes are rolled back; same engine is shown for shipments and edge infrastructure.
s2_notes: Strong video-backed design and visible explanatory page; live central interaction was not completed by the observer.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, impact, and creativity with coherent video evidence despite incomplete live interaction.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured controls over a real editor's shared project state, timeline analysis, preview, and FFmpeg export instead of requiring brittle UI clicking.
leverage_evidence: Submission lists seven tools spanning project state, settings, scenes, timeline analysis, preview, and render.
Claims calls enter the existing backend analysis and real FFmpeg export pipeline.
execution_rationale: The editor workspace and timeline controls loaded coherently, but loading the demo failed to produce a changed state and no edit, analysis, or export was verified live.
execution_evidence: Live observation saw media controls, preview, and empty timeline.
Landscape demo action yielded no usable post-action state or verified result.
impact_rationale: Agent control of precise edits in the same visible project can reduce repetitive production work while retaining human media and approval control, but demonstrated impact is limited by lack of execution proof.
impact_evidence: Submission describes shared visible editor state and human final approval.
Real playable MP4 export is claimed but not live verified.
creativity_rationale: Applying WebMCP to a full video editor and connecting agent actions to an existing render pipeline is useful and concrete, though the underlying workflow is a relatively direct structured-control adaptation.
creativity_evidence: Agent can inspect and modify project structure through named editor tools.
Claims integrate with an existing FFmpeg pipeline.
s2_notes: A coherent editor was visible, but the defining agent-driven edit/export loop remained unverified in observation.
advance_reason: Potential is good, but central edit and render execution was not demonstrated live.

leverage_rationale: The human's visual lasso is compiled into a revision-specific, typed WebMCP capability contract whose schemas restrict resources and authority; scope changes recompile the tools.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes selected resource IDs, constraints, and revision-specific schemas.
Video shows an out-of-scope driver request, human scope expansion, proof, expiring one-time execution, and stale-call rejection.
execution_rationale: The dispatch scenario and constraints were visible, but the observer could not define a scope or reach an agent result; no route execution was verified live.
execution_evidence: Live observation saw the seeded late-delivery scenario, no-overtime constraint, and changed-routes selector.
Reset interaction produced no usable post-action state.
impact_rationale: Turning an intuitive human boundary into enforceable structured agent authority is broadly valuable for dispatch, dashboards, CAD, and other high-consequence visual applications.
impact_evidence: Human-defined scope limits both readable resources and permitted changes.
Video claims protected routes remain untouched and stale calls are rejected.
creativity_rationale: The map-as-prompt and boundary-as-permission model is an especially original WebMCP interaction pattern: a transient visual gesture becomes a typed, revisioned capability surface.
creativity_evidence: Lasso compiles visual selection into schemas rather than merely highlighting it.
Agent cannot expand its own authority and execution is bound to exact scope and plan.
s2_notes: Video provides strong central-workflow evidence; live observer confirmed the setup but not drawing, repair, or execution.
advance_reason: Outstanding leverage, impact, and creativity, supported by a detailed workflow video.

leverage_rationale: The project exposes typed, page-scoped QA report and app controls so agents can consume structured verdicts, failures, and visual diffs instead of scraping screenshots or guessing controls.
leverage_evidence: Submission lists public report tools for summaries, visual changes, and failing steps plus a larger signed-in tool surface.
Tools are described as scoped to the visible page and backed by a polyfill.
execution_rationale: A public report page visibly provided a walkthrough, step navigation, visual-change notes, and before/after/diff controls, but the attempted step jump failed and full actions were login-gated.
execution_evidence: Live observation confirms coherent QA walkthrough and visual-diff reporting.
No changed playback state or full report action was verified; fuller access prompted sign-in.
impact_rationale: Making QA verdicts and failures directly queryable by a browser agent can materially improve release verification and reduce brittle visual scraping, especially for public reports and human review.
impact_evidence: Public report tools expose structured verdict/failure/diff data without login.
Submission connects the same site-tool model to run, review, and approval workflows.
creativity_rationale: The WebMCP integration is a practical and well-targeted extension of an existing QA product; it is valuable but less novel than projects that invent a new authority or collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Page tools mirror existing remote MCP functions while being scoped to what is on screen.
Report pages provide structured access to visual regression evidence.
s2_notes: Public report was live and coherent, but the browser could not verify tool calls or step navigation, and some capabilities were login-gated.
advance_reason: Clear practical leverage and impact with a functioning public report surface, despite incomplete interactive verification.

leverage_rationale: LaunchPad uses WebMCP to let an agent operate on the same stateful evidence workspace, including policy, privacy scope, evidence gaps, lineage, and human-consent boundaries.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes live workspace state shared between human and agent rather than a separate chat transcript.
Agent can research, challenge evidence, test policies, and trace recommendations to sources.
execution_rationale: The research workspace and problem form were visible, but the observer could not fill or start the run, so no evidence collection or recommendation state was verified.
execution_evidence: Live observation saw the problem brief form, research-factory panel, and research control.
Follow-up session could not locate the form/button and showed no research progress.
impact_rationale: Auditable, source-linked recommendations with counter-evidence and human approval could improve high-cost product and strategy decisions, though practical outcome is not demonstrated live.
impact_evidence: Submission promises lineage from source to finding, insight, feature, and recommendation.
Video explains closing evidence gaps, preserving counter-signals, and testing evidence policies.
creativity_rationale: The production-line framing of research, with explicit policy counterfactuals and full decision lineage inside a shared browser workspace, is a thoughtful extension beyond answer-generating agents.
creativity_evidence: Workspace tracks stages, gaps, evidence ledger, candidate, and version transitions.
Agent can show how changing evidence policy changes the recommendation.
s2_notes: Strong concept and explanatory video, but live research execution could not be initiated by the observer.
advance_reason: High-value auditable workflow with strong concept/video evidence, though runtime verification is incomplete.

leverage_rationale: LedgerRehearsal makes the page's WebMCP surface itself reflect human-reviewed authority: approval creates a scoped one-time execution capability, and changed reality revokes it.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes safe inspection/proposal/rehearsal tools, approval-dependent capability creation, revocation on drift, and one-time consumption.
Video transcript details exact proposed, authorized, executed, and blocked receipts.
execution_rationale: The live receivables workspace loaded with the claimed accounts and human review entry point, but review remained in a loading state and the full rehearsal/approval/execution sequence was not observed.
execution_evidence: Live observation confirms ACME, Jones, and Smith scenarios and Review proposed work control.
After click showed a preparing/loading state without the proposed-work result during the window.
impact_rationale: Rehearsing exact business effects and revoking stale approvals directly addresses safe agent action in changing real-world data, with clear auditability and human accountability.
impact_evidence: Payment sync invalidates a previously approved reminder in the demonstrated scenario.
Receipt distinguishes proposed, authorized, executed, and blocked changes.
creativity_rationale: Binding permission to a current factual rehearsal and changing the available WebMCP capability surface on approval or drift is a distinctive and elegant safety pattern.
creativity_evidence: Execution capability appears only after human review and disappears on stale state or successful use.
Agent supplies no replacement targets; page rechecks current state.
s2_notes: The live initial state matched the scenario; video transcript supplies detailed central workflow evidence, while live review loading prevented full confirmation.
advance_reason: Very strong safety leverage, impact, and creativity with detailed workflow evidence.

leverage_evidence: Submission lists four read-only tools for search, article retrieval, version comparison, and review-brief generation.

execution_evidence: Live observation saw statute/article/date/question fields populated coherently.

creativity_rationale: The historical statute-comparison workbench is a strong domain application of WebMCP, but the interaction pattern is primarily structured retrieval rather than a novel control model.
creativity_evidence: Archive-date-aware article comparison is tailored to Korean legal review.
Agent-generated brief preserves question, textual change, checks, and citations.

leverage_rationale: Lemma exposes a live structured document to an agent for surgical block edits, render-error inspection, equation/reference management, comments, and undo, eliminating copy-paste synchronization.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes 15 imperative tools plus a declarative form over a shared live document.
Video transcript shows the agent reading a render error, fixing one block, inserting labeled content, and commenting without changing mathematics.
execution_rationale: The live editor opened coherently with source, preview, export, comments, and WebMCP status, but New document did not visibly change state and no agent edit was observed.
execution_evidence: Live observation confirms a split live LaTeX workspace and tool-inspector/status framing.
New document action yielded no visible template chooser or new document.
impact_rationale: Shared live structure and immediate render feedback can materially reduce technical-writing iteration errors while keeping changes targeted, attributed, and undoable.
impact_evidence: Video demonstrates repair of a typo, numbered equation insertion, reference resolution, and margin comment.
Submission emphasizes author control and targeted undoable changes.
creativity_rationale: Treating a mathematical document as structured blocks with identities, render status, references, and comments is a strong and domain-aware WebMCP collaboration model.
creativity_evidence: Agent edits individual blocks rather than replacing a stale text snapshot.
Equation numbering and labels remain live and references resolve after insertion.
s2_notes: Video strongly demonstrates the central editor/agent loop; live observer confirmed the workspace but not an agent edit.
advance_reason: Strongly demonstrated practical collaboration with high leverage and impact.

leverage_rationale: The agent plays through constrained sensor readings and can rewrite the hunter bot's code mid-match, making WebMCP part of the game mechanics rather than a peripheral control layer.
leverage_evidence: Submission describes one-second sensor readings, a full rulebook tool, and agent rewriting the built-in seeker's code.
The game design lets model intelligence improve behavior over time rather than simply issuing a move.
execution_rationale: The game screen loaded, but power controls were disabled and the observer could not start a match or obtain a briefing result, so gameplay and code rewriting were not verified.
execution_evidence: Live observation saw the dark game screen, sound control, disabled power buttons, and instruction control.
No playable match or briefing result appeared in the captured state.
impact_rationale: The project has entertainment and research value as an experiment in agent gameplay and self-improving behavior, but broader practical impact is limited and live operation was not shown.
impact_evidence: Submission frames a three-minute hide-and-seek challenge with bounded sensing.
The claimed outcome is an interactive game rather than a high-stakes workflow.
creativity_rationale: A real-time hide-and-seek game where the agent rewrites its hunter code during the chase is an imaginative, distinctive use of WebMCP with meaningful game-design integration.
creativity_evidence: Human sees the full world while the agent receives sparse sensing.
Agent can improve the bot through code changes during the match.
s2_notes: Distinctive game concept and live shell, but the central match was not playable in the observation.
advance_reason: Creativity is high, but execution and practical impact are weakly verified.

leverage_rationale: LINECALL gives the agent structured schedule reasoning, constraint checking, exact cue-level previews, and a separate approval-gated apply action instead of uncontrolled timing edits.
leverage_evidence: Submission lists tools for reading run state, comparing strategies, preparing previews, updating readiness, and applying only after approval.
The claimed demo rejects a chronology-breaking local move and prepares a safer 13-cue ripple.
execution_rationale: The live landing page clearly communicated the workflow, but Enter the live desk did not navigate to a working desk and no schedule change was observed.
execution_evidence: Live observation confirms coherent landing copy and live-desk entry path.
Captured page remained on landing with no live desk state.
impact_rationale: Safe timing analysis for live events can prevent cascading production failures while retaining operator approval, making the workflow consequential in practice.
impact_evidence: Submission describes downstream ripple analysis across speakers, video, lighting, audio, and cues.

creativity_rationale: Combining constraint-aware schedule reasoning with a previewed ripple plan and one-time human approval is a thoughtful WebMCP pattern for live production.
creativity_evidence: Agent explores, rules verify, human approves, and agent acts once.
The system rejects a seemingly simpler segment-only change when chronology would break.
s2_notes: Landing page matched the stated workflow, but the live desk and central schedule operation were not reachable in observation.
advance_reason: High-value and coherent safety workflow, with incomplete runtime verification.

execution_rationale: The manager workspace loaded coherently with Sophie selected and grounded HR data, but the attempted employee switch did not change state and no agent draft was observed.
execution_evidence: Live observation saw roster, goals, actions, skill signals, and waiting-for-agent timeline.

impact_rationale: Grounded development-conversation preparation could save managerial time and improve consistency while preserving human decision authority, but the sensitive HR workflow was not live-executed here.
impact_evidence: Submission describes topics grounded in current goals, actions, and skill signals.

creativity_rationale: State-aware capability changes and shared HR context are a thoughtful application, though the core pattern is a fairly direct structured retrieval-and-drafting workflow.
creativity_evidence: Capabilities are scoped to manager authority and employee context.
